analysis: What changed vs the 6:00 AM brief: the open confirmed the split tape (Nasdaq +0.43%, S&P +0.24%, Dow -0.03%) but the stock-level story got stricter, not softer. The morning's two big earnings winners diverged in the regular session: Vertiv held most of its pop (+13.9% early vs +16% premarket), while GE Vernova swung from a +3-4% premarket gain to -5.5% in early trading despite beating, raising guidance, and announcing a $9B Trench acquisition. Paired with Seagate deepening to -6.5% (from -3.3% premarket) on its own beat, the message is now unmistakable: this tape is selling good quarters when the run is already priced in, and the only names holding gains are the memory chain (SK Hynix +8%, Micron +4%, SanDisk +3-5%), where the demand evidence is newest. Megacaps are flat by design — nobody wants size ahead of the Fed at 2:00 p.m. ET and Microsoft/Alphabet after the close. Signal: the AI-infrastructure demand chain keeps beating across memory, cooling, and power, and the memory leg is actually being bought. Noise: single-stock early-session percentages (GEV whipsawed twice before the open), the still-unconfirmed Houthi refinery strike claim behind oil's premium, and any pre-read of Warsh's press conference. USAC note: MarketBeat lists Q3 earnings for Nov 4 while the company's own release says before the open Nov 3 — worth confirming, company release governs.
disclaimer: Not financial advice — for informational purposes only.

headlines.headline: A split open: Nasdaq Composite +0.43%, S&P 500 +0.24%, Dow -0.03% at the start of Wednesday's session, per TokenPost's open read (published 6:35 AM PT).
headlines.why_it_matters: Tech leads and blue chips lag into a Fed day — the tape is positioned for tonight's events, not running ahead of them.

headlines.headline: Memory leads the early session: SK Hynix's US-listed shares +8.11% after record Q3 results (revenue 104.6T won, operating profit 83.3T won, demand seen outstripping supply through 2030), Micron +3.9-4.4% and SanDisk +3.4-5.0% in early trading; South Korea's KOSPI closed +6.6-6.7%.
headlines.why_it_matters: The memory leg of the AI trade is being bought in the regular session, not just premarket — fresh demand evidence, not just a headline pop.

headlines.headline: Vertiv holds most of its pop, +13.9% in early trading (vs +16% premarket) after its Q3 blowout: EPS $2.21 vs $1.82 expected, revenue +60.8% to $4.31B, Q4 guide above consensus.
headlines.why_it_matters: Cooling/power is the one AI-infrastructure winner still being rewarded after the open — the exception that proves the strict-grading rule.

headlines.headline: Seagate deepens its sell-the-beat slide to -6.5% in early trading (vs -3.3% premarket) despite fiscal Q1 EPS $7.68 vs $7.42 expected, revenue +60%+ to $4.23B, and guidance ahead of the Street; shares were up ~150% for the year into the print.
headlines.why_it_matters: A beat that sells off harder once regular trading starts — the bar for tonight's Microsoft and Alphabet prints keeps rising.

headlines.headline: GE Vernova reverses from a +3-4% premarket gain to -5.5% in early trading despite beating (Q3 EPS $4.81 vs ~$4.01 expected, revenue $12.64B, +27% year over year), orders up 96% to $29.3B, backlog $197B, raised 2026 guidance ($46.5-47.5B revenue), and a $9B cash-and-debt deal to buy grid-equipment maker Trench Group.
headlines.why_it_matters: The sharpest sell-the-beat of the morning — even a beat, a raise, and a deal together couldn't hold the gain, so good quarters alone aren't enough right now.

headlines.headline: Robinhood falls 8.4% in early trading after its Q3 miss: revenue +12% to $1.42B, but adjusted EPS $0.60 missed as expenses climbed and crypto revenue plunged 55% to $120M; bitcoin is down ~28% over three months.
headlines.why_it_matters: A genuine miss, not profit-taking — crypto weakness is now a visible drag on a retail-trading bellwether.

headlines.headline: Megacaps mostly flat into tonight's prints: Alphabet +1.2% premarket ahead of Q3 after the close (consensus ~$128B revenue, ~$2.94-3.03 EPS, Google Cloud near $29.15B); Microsoft -0.1% early ahead of fiscal Q1 after the close (consensus ~$90.6B revenue, ~$4.71-4.73 EPS, Azure growth near 44.8%). Nvidia -0.2%, Apple -0.5%, Amazon +0.1% early; Tesla +0.6% premarket.
headlines.why_it_matters: Nobody is taking size into the Fed decision plus two cloud prints — flat megacaps are a waiting posture, and cloud growth plus AI capex matter more than headline EPS after this morning's sell-the-beats.

headlines.headline: The Fed decision lands at 2:00 p.m. ET with Chair Warsh's press conference at 2:30 p.m. ET; a hold at 3.75-4.00% is priced at roughly 90-93%, while December hike odds sit at 86% per CME FedWatch.
headlines.why_it_matters: A hold is priced in, so December guidance is the trade — and firming December odds plus oil above $101 keep the hawkish-steer risk live.

headlines.headline: Oil holds its premium but off the highs: Brent ~$115.5 (+1.4%) and WTI ~$101.3-101.9 (+1.4-2.0%) after Yemen's Houthis said they hit Saudi Arabia's Ras Tanura refinery (550,000 barrels/day) with a missile; Saudi authorities have not confirmed the strike or any damage. The EIA inventory report lands at 10:30 a.m. ET after API data showed a 2.03M-barrel draw.
headlines.why_it_matters: A supply-risk premium is back in crude hours before the Fed decision — single-source, unconfirmed on the strike itself, so treat the geopolitical leg as fragile even as the price move is real.

usac.why_it_matters: No fresh USAC company news this morning. The Q3 distribution of $0.525 per common unit ($2.10 annualized) pays Nov 6 to holders of record Oct 26. Q3 earnings: the company's own release schedules them before the open Tue Nov 3 with an 11 a.m. ET call, but MarketBeat's earnings calendar now lists Nov 4 — the company date governs unless USAC updates it. Last reported quarter (Q2, Aug 4): EPS $0.31 beat the $0.28 consensus, revenue $342.15M vs $340.49M expected. WTI holding above $101 on the Saudi refinery headlines keeps the energy backdrop supportive with no company-specific catalyst.
